provenance.method: Question assembled from reviewed games where modes materially change objectives, pressure or creative freedom. Mode distinctions are preserved instead of assigning a single 'relaxing' label to the whole product.

question: Which games let me choose a lower-pressure mode instead of making the whole game low-pressure?
why_it_matters: A game can contain both demanding and low-demand modes; treating the title as one fixed experience can hide the setting or mode that actually determines fit.
current_understanding: Minecraft changes substantially by mode and settings. Minami Lane separates objective-driven missions from a sandbox mode focused on creativity. Cloud Gardens combines puzzle progression with a creative mode. These examples show why ND Oracle should route by mode and mechanic rather than genre or a blanket 'cozy' tag.
evidence_needed: Platform-specific accessibility and mode documentation for more games, including whether settings can be changed mid-session and what progress systems remain active.
reopening_conditions: A listed game's modes or accessibility settings materially change.
A governed game-facet model can represent mode-specific pressure directly rather than in prose.
dissent: A mode marketed as sandbox or creative can still contain sensory, motor or cognitive demands; lower objective pressure is only one dimension of access.
